title: Enterprise prospect playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch guidance, pricing & security FAQ
author: Jordan Patel
summary: A consolidated enterprise prospect playbook that equips field sellers and solutions engineers with positioning & messaging, competitive briefing, pitch deck slide guidance, pricing guardrails, short case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Intended for AE/SE motions targeting mid-market and enterprise buyers evaluating LLM inference platforms.
body:
Overview:

This playbook is a single-page reference for enterprise prospect engagements. It bundles succinct positioning for discovery, a competitive brief with recommended battlecards, a standard slide outline for in-person/demo pitches, concrete pricing guardrails and line items to preview during procurement, short case-study bullets that resonate with different buyer personas, and a security FAQ for prospects. Use this during qualification, discovery calls, technical workshops, and procurement conversations.

1) Key positioning and messaging (elevator and discovery hooks):
- Elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical at production scale - across hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments for regulated workloads.
- Value props to emphasize by persona:
  - Engineering / ML Infra: predictable latency & throughput, per-route observability, intelligent batching, and smooth model rollouts.
  - Product / App teams: consistent API across environments, fast prototyping with hosted API, predictable unit economics as usage grows.
  - Security / Legal / Compliance: VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs and evidence for compliance.
- Discovery questions:
  1. What are your latency and throughput targets (p95 latency, tokens/sec)?
  2. Do you need private network connectivity or on-prem for regulated data?
  3. What is your expected monthly token/embedding volume in year-1/year-2?
  4. How important is model version pinning and canary rollouts for you?

2) Competitive brief (short-form battlecard) - talking points and differentiation:
- Competitor set (typical): Cloud-managed endpoints (C1), LLM API providers (C2), self-hosted inference runtimes (C3).
- Primary differentiators: production-first runtime, unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, cost-aware knobs (batching, cache, quantization profiles), built-in fallback routing & SLA-backed Dedicated offering.

Competitor comparison (summary table):
| Feature / Dimension | Redwood Inference | Cloud-managed endpoints (C1) | LLM API providers (C2) | Self-hosted runtimes (C3) |
|---------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------|
| Deployment modes    | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted only / limited Private | Hosted only | Private only (customer infra) |
| SLA & reserved capacity | Yes (Dedicated) | Varies, often no committed capacity | No | Depends on implementation |
| Observability & cost breakdown | Token-level + per-route dashboards | Limited | Varies | Mostly custom |
| Rollouts & fallbacks | Canary, A/B, automatic fallbacks | Limited | No | Custom tooling |
| Security & compliance | VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs | Cloud-native controls | Varies | Customer-managed |
| Cost controls (batching/caching) | Smart batching + caching suggestions | Limited | Not exposed | Implementation-dependent |

Battlecard quick rebuttals:
- If prospect says "we can use cloud endpoints": emphasize Dedicated capacity for predictable performance and cost, and Private options for regulated data.
- If seller hears "we can self-host to save cost": call out total-cost-of-ownership - engineering ops, kernel optimizations, observability, and SRE overhead. Redwood reduces time-to-prod and ongoing operational cost.

3) Pitch deck & demo structure (recommended slide + demo outline):
- Slide 1: Title + one-line positioning (customized to prospect)
- Slide 2: Why inference economics matter (latency, cost, reliability) - short customer metrics (tokens/sec, % cost savings)
- Slide 3: Redwood at a glance (hosted, dedicated, private) + one-line differentiator per mode
- Slide 4: Architecture (high-level runtime, caching, routing, private control plane) - single diagram
- Slide 5: Observability & SLOs (screenshots: per-route dashboard, token-level cost)
- Slide 6: Security & compliance (networking, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO evidence pointers)
- Slide 7: Pricing approach & suggested pilot package (see Pricing Guidance)
- Slide 8: Customer stories (2 short case bullets)
- Slide 9: Next steps & checklist (technical workshop, POC KPIs, SOW template)

Demo plan (20-30 minutes):
1. Quick app walkthrough showing latency & token cost in console (3 min)
2. Live inference demo: hosted API + show fallback to dedicated/private model (6-8 min)
3. Observability walkthrough: trace a slow request, show per-route cost (5 min)
4. Q&A + ops conversation: deployment options, network setup, SLA (5-10 min)

4) Pricing guidance & procurement guardrails (public-facing starter guidance for AEs):
- Pricing model: usage-based for Hosted (per-token generation/embedding), committed monthly/annual contracts for Dedicated (capacity units), enterprise licensing for Private (platform fee + support).
- Pilot offer (standard): 3-month pilot, up to 5M tokens/month on Hosted with optional Dedicated evaluation window. Includes onboarding support and two solution-engineer workshops.
- Typical enterprise band examples (ballpark ranges for negotiation):
  - Small enterprise pilot: $25k-75k (3 months, advisory & support)
  - Mid enterprise annual commit: $100k-500k (includes reserved Dedicated capacity blocks and support tier)
  - Large enterprise / regulated: $500k+ (Private deployment, dedicated onboarding, custom SLAs)
- Pricing levers to discuss with procurement: committed capacity level, retention/observability retention add-ons, premium SLA, on-prem packaging.

Pricing table (example / simplified):
| Item | Description | Typical list | Negotiation levers |
|------|-------------|--------------|--------------------|
| Hosted usage | Per-token generation/embedding | $0.000X per token (varies by model) | Commit volume, model tiers |
| Dedicated | Reserved capacity blocks (GPU-hours equivalent) | Monthly commit $k-50k+ | Burst capacity, priority routing |
| Private | On-prem/VPC license + support | Platform fee + integration | Deployment scope, support level |

5) Case studies (concise bullets to use in pitch):
- Fintech customer (mid-market): Reduced per-token cost by 42% after switching to Dedicated with intelligent batching; p95 latency met 150ms target; outcome: enabled real-time credit decisioning feature.
- Enterprise knowledge base (large SaaS): Deployed Private control plane for customer data residency; integrated KMS and audit logs to pass SOC2 audit with no major findings.
- Marketplace startup (growth): Used Hosted API for rapid feature launch then migrated hot routes to Dedicated to save 30% on unit costs while retaining low latency.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for AE/SE use):
Q: Where is our customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Default: Hosted customers have data retention policy configurable; we provide retention controls and redaction options. For Dedicated and Private, customers retain full control and logs are kept per contract (we recommend 90-365 days depending on compliance needs).

Q: What encryption do you support?
A: Data in transit TLS 1.2+; data at rest encrypted using AES-256. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations.

Q: Can we run the control plane in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes - Redwood Private provides a customer-managed control plane option and an on-prem packaging path for air-gapped deployments. See reference architecture in related pages.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and compliance evidence?
A: Yes - audit logging is included for Dedicated and Private. We provide SOC/ISO evidence packages to enterprise customers under NDA; see security-and-compliance runbook for evidence process.

Q: How do you protect against model-output data leakage?
A: We offer prompt and output redaction controls, model isolation by tenant, optional in-flight KV masking, and monitoring for anomalous output patterns as part of our quality-guardrails.

Q: Who has access to customer data?
A: Access is role-based (RBAC) and audited. For Hosted we follow least-privilege operations model; for Dedicated and Private customers can require additional controls and restrict vendor access per contract.

7) Common objections and suggested responses:
- "We already have cloud endpoints": "Great - many customers start there; Redwood helps when you need predictable capacity, cost control, and richer observability/rollout tooling. We can run a short pilot to compare TCO and performance metrics."
- "Self-hosting is cheaper": "Self-hosting often transfers cost to engineering and SRE teams. We provide optimized kernels, continuous batching, and managed observability that reduces time-to-value and ongoing ops burden."
- "Security is a blocker": "We offer Private deployments, VPC control plane options, and KMS integrations. We’ll run a security workshop and share compliance artifacts under NDA."

8) Playbook actions & checklist for AE/SE before a procurement call (numbered):
1. Confirm target latency, throughput, and retention requirements.
2. Prepare estimated monthly token volume and expected growth.
3. Identify required compliance artifacts and who will own review (security team contact).
4. Decide pilot scope (models, routes, SLA expectations).
5. Prepare draft SOW with pilot pricing and success metrics.

9) Appendix: resources and ownership
- SE playbook owner: Jordan Patel (go-to-market)
- Security collateral owner: Priya Desai (security)
- Reference pages: see related_pages list above for decks, SOW templates, and architecture reference.

Usage notes: keep messaging concise and tailored by persona; when in doubt, prioritize production economics (latency/cost/reliability) over model feature claims. Always route security or legal questions to Priya Desai and technical ops to Michael Zhang.
talking_points: Emphasize unified API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private: fewer code paths for product teams.
Lead with production economics: measurable cost and latency improvements are the fastest path to buy-in.
Use case-specific case studies: fintech for latency/throughput, enterprise KB for compliance, marketplace for cost optimization.
Offer a short pilot with clear KPIs and success criteria to de-risk procurement.
pricing_guidance: Pilot: 3 months, up to 5M tokens/month, includes onboarding and 2 workshops. Typical enterprise ranges: Small pilot $25k-75k; Mid enterprise annual commit $100k-500k; Large/regulated $500k+. Key levers: committed capacity, retention add-ons, premium SLA.
competitor_matrix: See competitor comparison table in body for short feature-by-feature summary. Focus rebuttals: total cost of ownership vs self-host; committed capacity / SLA vs cloud endpoints; observability & rollout tooling vs generic APIs.
case_studies: Fintech: 42% cost reduction after Dedicated migration; p95 latency 150ms; enabled real-time credit decisions.
Enterprise KB: Private deployment + KMS achieved SOC2 compliance with no major findings.
Marketplace startup: Hosted -> Dedicated migration resulted in 30% unit cost savings while preserving latency.
security_faq: Where is data stored and retention? - Hosted configurable retention; Dedicated/Private under customer control (recommended 90-365 days).
Encryption? - TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest; customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private.
VPC/on-prem control plane? - Yes, available via Redwood Private and on-prem packaging.
Audit logs & compliance evidence? - Included for Dedicated/Private; SOC/ISO evidence available under NDA.
Model-output leakage protections? - Prompt/output redaction, model isolation, KV masking options, anomalous-output monitoring.
Who has access to data? - RBAC + audited access; additional contractual restrictions available for Dedicated/Private.
